reading_purpose: This note is a FRAME CONTEST, not a discriminant application. The survey is read to answer four questions: (a) how its three axes cut the same literature against the monograph's three layers and three paths; (b) how it classifies Nested Learning, against ch18's verdict; (c) whether it registers the cost-reporting vacuum that X3 established; (d) which papers it treats as important that the monograph corpus lacks.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: The field has many memory mechanisms and no common frame. 'Despite this rapid progress, the literature lacks a unified perspective elucidating the conceptual relationships among these disparate memory mechanisms. Attention-based caching, recurrent sequence states, test-time adaptation, retrieval modules, and conditional parameter routing are frequently studied in isolation, even though they address fundamentally isomorphic questions: what is stored, when and how it is updated, how it interacts with forward computation, its retention duration, and its underlying storage granularity. Without a principled structural framework, comparing methodologies, analyzing system-level trade-offs, and identifying unexplored design spaces remain profoundly difficult.' [§I, p.1]
problem_stated.the_historical_claim: 'Historically, memory in neural language models was predominantly implicit.' ... 'More recently, a distinct architectural shift has emerged... an increasing number of studies incorporate explicit and persistent memory mechanisms that adaptively evolve beyond ephemeral inference' [§I, pp.1-2]. The claimed transition: 'memory is transitioning into a primary, explicit architectural design dimension rather than remaining a mere byproduct of scaling.' [§I, p.1]
problem_stated.the_scope_it_draws: TWICE, and both exclusions are load-bearing for this note. (i) 'In this survey, we focus specifically on model-level memory mechanisms and systems, i.e., memory that is instantiated within the model architecture or its inference-time dynamics, and exclude agent-level or prompt-based memory systems that rely on external orchestration or engineering pipelines.' [§II preamble, p.2]. (ii) 'In this survey, we do not discuss static model parameters learned during pretraining (e.g., the weights of attention or MLP layers), even though they encode knowledge.' [§II-A-c 'Scope Clarification', pp.2-3]. Restated in §IV: 'we focus strictly on model-level explicit memory mechanisms. We do not consider prompt-level memory engineering, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, or external agent frameworks that rely on databases or orchestration systems.' [§IV preamble, p.9]
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] The two exclusions between them delete two of the monograph's three paths before the taxonomy is even applied. Exclusion (i) removes the entire E-path (Letta STC, MemGPT, Mem0, Zep, ReasoningBank, SCM, RAG). Exclusion (ii), reinforced by §IV-E-f ('this survey does not treat continual-learning optimizers as a primary memory architecture', p.13), removes the entire Theta-path (SEAL, `LM Need Sleep`, LoRA, ROME/MEMIT). What remains in scope is the W-path — and the survey's primary axis then SPLITS the W-path down the middle. See axis_contrast_with_book.

inherited_open_question.bridge_in_material: [note-writer] For the monograph this table is directly useful in ch01 and ch11: it is an outside enumeration of the axes the field has already tried, and NONE of the six (including this one) uses 'when does the update happen relative to the query' as an axis. This is external evidence that the monograph's three-layer split is not a redescription of an existing taxonomy.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: The survey's 'mechanism' is a labelling function, not an update rule. It assigns each system a triple tau(P) = (representation, update-dynamics, persistence) in {implicit, explicit} x {offline, online} x {short-term, long-term}, plus a secondary five-valued update-rule tag. It changes no layer, spends no budget, and reports no measurement; under the monograph's frame it modifies neither Theta, W, nor E.

the_only_numbered_equation_in_the_paper.paper_number: Eq. (1) — the sole NUMBERED equation in 20 pages [§IV-C, p.12, L1641-1645]. Two further unnumbered expressions appear inside Fig. 3 (p.7): the linear-attention state update and the SSM recurrence $h_t = A_t h_{t-1} + B_t x_t$. Those are figure labels, not text, and one of them collides with a reserved symbol — see notation_conflicts and todo_verify T3.
the_only_numbered_equation_in_the_paper.paper_form: y = sum_{i in S(h)} g_i(h) * Expert_i(h), where S(h) is a small selected subset and g_i(h) is the gating weight
the_only_numbered_equation_in_the_paper.gloss: MoE sparse gating. Under the monograph frame this is a READ, not a write: it is a special case of $f(\cdot)$ in (R) with a data-dependent sparse mask over frozen $\Theta$. Nothing on the right-hand side changes between queries. The survey nonetheless calls the expert bank 'a distinct form of offline explicit memory embedded in parameter space' [§IV-C, p.12]. This single equation is the clearest instance of the deep difference between the two frames: the survey admits read-side addressing into 'memory'; the monograph's discriminant condition (3) requires a state change.

representation.implicit: 'information that is stored as a byproduct of the model's forward computation and is tightly coupled with its internal dynamics. Such memory does not expose an explicit read, write or lookup interface; instead, it is accessed implicitly through the computation graph.' Examples given: recurrent states (RNN, linear attention, SSM) and KV caches. 'Although some implicit memory structures (e.g., KV caches) are materialized as explicit tensors, their access semantics are fixed by the model architecture and lack independent addressing or update control.' [§II-A-a, p.2]
representation.explicit: 'instantiated as a distinct storage component with well-defined access semantics. It typically supports explicit addressing, retrieval, and update operations that are not reducible to standard forward computation or offline backpropagation... Notably, explicit memory is not restricted to non-parametric structures... What distinguishes them from standard model parameters is not their parametric form, but the fact that they are designed and operated as memory, with clear read/write semantics and controllable update policies.' [§II-A-b, p.2]
representation.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] The operative criterion is 'designed and operated as memory' — DESIGN INTENT, not mechanism. The survey itself flags the instability of this criterion; see unfavorable_facts F1.

update_dynamics.offline: 'Offline memory systems are updated only during a distinct model training phase, typically via gradient-based optimization. Once training is complete, the memory remains fixed during inference.' [§II-B-a, pp.3-4]. Fig. 2's one-line gloss: 'Offline: Updates during training only (Pretraining, MoE)' [Fig. 2, p.3]
update_dynamics.online: 'Online memory systems support updates during inference, allowing the model to incorporate new information on the fly. Such updates may be triggered at various frequencies: per token, per segment, or per batch, and can be governed by specialized rules distinct from standard backpropagation.' [§II-B-b, p.4]. Fig. 2: 'Online: Updates during inference (TTT, Recurrent States)' [Fig. 2, p.3]
update_dynamics.DECISIVE_FINDING: [note-writer] The survey's 'offline' means TRAINING-TIME. It does not mean 'before the query arrives'. The three frequencies it enumerates for online updates — per token, per segment, per batch — are all DURING a request. There is no third value and no cell for 'at deployment, but before q'. Sleep-time compute, in every one of its three paths, is 'online' under this axis, in the same cell as a Mamba state transition. This axis therefore cannot express the monograph's subject at all. It is the single most important cross-frame fact in this note.

persistence.short_term: 'stores information at relatively fine granularity and is typically bounded to a local context window, segment, or inference episode.' [§II-C-a, p.5]
persistence.long_term: 'designed to preserve information or its influence over extended contexts, and in some cases across sessions. It does not necessarily require a large uncompressed store. Recurrent sequence memory, for example, may maintain only a fixed-size state, but this state acts as a compressed summary whose receptive field can span very long sequences... long-term memory is characterized by an extended effective horizon, often enabled by higher compression, selective retention, or persistent storage, rather than by storage size alone.' [§II-C-b, p.5]
persistence.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] Under this definition 'long-term' means 'unbounded receptive field in principle', NOT 'survives the session'. That is why Mamba is Long-Term and why 37 of the 47 tabulated systems are Long-Term. The label carries no persistence claim, which matters when reading the survey's Long-Term tag on Nested Learning (see nested_learning_classification).

the_taxonomy_stated_verbatim.orthogonality_claim: 'These three axes are largely orthogonal. For instance, explicit memory can be either offline or online, and online memory may exhibit either short-term or long-term persistence depending on its update and eviction policies.' [§II-C-c, p.5]. This claim is falsified by the survey's own Table I — see unfavorable_facts F3.

the_secondary_update_rule_axis_TableII.preamble: 'The offline/online distinction specifies when memory can be modified, but it does not fully characterize how the memory content is updated... We therefore treat update rules as a secondary lens within the update-dynamics axis' [§II-B-c, pp.4-5]. Table II (p.5) has five rows. This is the part of the survey that the monograph does NOT have and could productively absorb (see axis_contrast_with_book.where_the_survey_cuts_better).

No formal framework, despite the abstract's 'We further formalize the granular mechanisms dictating memory writing, routing, state transitions, and consolidation.' The 'formalization' is Table II's five prose descriptions. §VI-A then asks for exactly this as future work — see unfavorable_facts F5.
No sleep, no idle-time compute, no pre-query computation. Whole-text counts: 'sleep' 0, 'Sleep' 0, 'idle' 0, 'prefetch' 0, 'amortiz/amortis' 0, 'test-time compute' 0, 'inference scaling' 0.
No biology. Whole-text counts: 'hippocamp' 0, 'McClelland' 0, 'replay' 0, 'dream' 0, 'biolog' 0, 'consolidation' 11 (all architectural: KV consolidation, memory consolidation as an update-rule name).

cost_table.preamble: All four cells are absent, and the absence is total rather than partial: this survey reports no measurement of any kind. That is expected of a survey and is not a criticism per se. What IS reportable is (i) that the survey names cost as a desideratum three separate times without ever giving a unit, and (ii) that its axis set has no coordinate that could hold $B_s$ even in principle.

B_s.detail: Not merely unreported — inexpressible. $B_s$ is a budget spent between requests; the survey's update-dynamics axis has two values, training-time and inference-time, and no notion of a request boundary. The word 'budget' occurs three times and never in this sense: 'cache budget' [§II-C-a, p.5], 'implicit memory budget' [§III-B-a, p.7], 'A related fixed-budget precursor' [§V-A-b, p.15] — all three mean a storage allowance, not a compute allowance.
B_s.consequence_for_X3: X3's finding (of 29 corpus papers, exactly 1 reports $B_s$ in absolute units) is untouched. This paper adds a 30th data point of a different kind: a 2026 survey of 47 memory systems that does not ask the question.

L_w.detail: Zero latency numbers. The word 'latency' appears once, in a future-work wish: 'Such co-design efforts will be essential for sustaining scalability without prohibitive energy or latency costs.' [§VI-E, p.18]. §V-B discusses PagedAttention [82] and CommVQ [81] entirely qualitatively — no ms, no TTFT, no tokens/s, no memory-footprint number.

C_cap.detail: No byte, no parameter count, no slot count anywhere. The survey's persistence axis is defined explicitly to be independent of storage size — 'long-term memory... does not necessarily require a large uncompressed store' [§II-C-b, p.5] — so the axis that looks like a capacity axis is deliberately not one. §IV-E-a states the qualitative scaling relation only: 'explicit memory may scale with the number of parameters, slots, or datastore entries. Lookup-based systems can grow unbounded as new entries accumulate' [p.13].
C_cap.the_one_symbolic_exception: Fig. 3 (p.7) annotates the recurrent state's SHAPE: 'Memory Size - d_v x d_k' for linear attention and 'Memory Size - d x N' for SSMs [vendored L1004, L1029]. This is the survey's only capacity statement of any kind. It gives the tensor shape and no dtype and no number, so it yields no byte count — but it is more than the corpus's E-path papers give, and ch26 should note that the $W$-layer literature at least states the shape while the $E$-layer literature states nothing.
C_cap.one_new_capacity_REGIME_the_monograph_la: Engram is described as introducing 'a scalable addressing substrate whose capacity can grow independently from dense computation, subject to the accuracy and collision behavior of the indexing scheme' [§IV-B-c, p.12]. This is capacity that is GLOBAL and SHARED, not per-session or per-user. The monograph's $C_{\text{cap}}$ is defined in bytes/session or bytes/user (S0 §2.4), which cannot express it. See book_impact ch26.

rho.detail: No degradation measurement. The survey does name the phenomenon repeatedly and well: 'In parameterized modules updated at test time, rapid adaptation risks destabilizing learned representations. In lookup-based systems, stale or redundant entries may bias retrieval.' [§IV-E-b, p.13]; 'these mechanisms also reintroduce classical challenges of continual learning, including forgetting and instability under distribution shift.' [§VI-B, p.17]; 'once a token or memory entry is dropped, compressed, or overwritten, later retrieval may be impossible' [§VI-C, p.17]. All three are assertions about the field, with no citation to a measurement and no measurement of its own.
rho.note: [note-writer] §VI-C's irreversibility statement is the closest external articulation of the flaw ch14 identifies in Letta STC's destructive $\mathrm{wr}$ (App. K: the new string 'replaces the current context'). Quotable in ch14 and ch30 as convergent, independent naming of the same failure mode in a different system class.

N_q.value: absent — and the concept does not appear. No amortisation, no queries-per-context, no request model. The survey has no notion of a query stream at all; its unit of analysis is the forward pass.

axis_contrast_with_book.headline: The two frames barely touch. Of the monograph's 29 corpus papers the survey cites 3 (Nested Learning [11], Memory Caching [37] by arXiv ID; Memorizing Transformers [73] via its OpenReview entry), and only 2 of those appear in its taxonomy table. Of the monograph's three paths, the survey excludes $E$ by declared scope and $\Theta$ by declared scope, and then splits the surviving path, $W$, across the two values of its own primary axis. Symmetrically, the monograph has no coordinate for the thing the survey's primary axis measures — whether the store is independently addressable — so the survey's whole lookup/routing family (kNN-LM, PlugLM, Engram, ExplicitLM, MoE) is invisible in the monograph's frame. Each axis is blind exactly where the other is sharp.

the_two_partitions_stated_precisely.survey: tau(P) = (representation, update-dynamics, persistence) in {implicit, explicit} x {offline, online} x {short-term, long-term}, where offline = 'updated only during a distinct model training phase' and online = 'updates during inference... per token, per segment, or per batch'. Secondary tag: one of five update rules (Table II). Unit of analysis: the forward pass.
the_two_partitions_stated_precisely.book: delta(P) in {pass, boundary, fail} by the four-condition discriminant (before $q$ / $B_s>0$ / a layer's state actually changes / the change is used by later queries), then for the passers ell(P) in {Theta, W, E} by which of (U-Theta)/(U-W)/(U-E) is instantiated, then a four-number cost vector ($B_s$, $L_w$, $C_{\text{cap}}$, $\rho$). Unit of analysis: the query stream.

The two that would be IN scope — `Do LMs Need Sleep?` (2605.26099, a W-path recurrence method) and SEAL (2506.10943, in-scope only if one reads self-edits as a writable module) — are simply absent from an 85-reference bibliography.
same_paper_different_cell.which_cuts_better: [평가] Not a resolution question. This is the finding: the mechanism-level memory-architecture community as represented by this survey does not know the sleep-time-compute literature exists. The word 'sleep' occurs zero times in 20 pages. ch11 and ch23 both need this.

where_the_book_cuts_better: TIMING. The monograph's condition (1) — before $q$ arrives — is the axis the survey does not have and cannot construct from its own coordinates. Every sleep-time method in all three paths falls into the survey's 'online' cell alongside a per-token Mamba state update. An axis that cannot separate 'a background job that ran last night' from 'a state transition on this token' cannot support any cost argument at all.

MECHANISM OVER INTENT. Explicit-vs-implicit is decided by whether a store is 'designed and operated as memory' [§II-A-b, p.2]. That is a statement about the authors, not about the computation, and it breaks under reduction ([72], §IV-A-c). $\Theta$/$W$/$E$ is decided by where the bytes live and which update equation applies, which does not break.

COST. The monograph demands four numbers per paper and records 'absent' when they are missing; that discipline is what produced X3's finding. The survey demands none, records none, and therefore cannot notice that the field reports none.

FALSIFICATION. The survey reports every method by its own claims. It contains no negative result, no ablation reversal, no unfavorable fact about any cited paper, and no instance of a baseline beating a method. The monograph's obligatory-caveat discipline (PRE-RESEARCH §4, 30 entries) has no counterpart here.

AXIS RESOLUTION. The survey's three binary axes resolve 47 systems into 5 non-empty cells, two of which hold 29 of them (implicit/online/long = 19, explicit/offline/long = 10). The discriminant resolves 29 papers into 9/1/19 and then the passers into 3 paths of 6/1/2. Per paper classified, the discriminant separates more.
where_the_survey_cuts_better: READ-SIDE STRUCTURE — the monograph's most serious gap. The monograph's read equation (R) hides all addressing inside $f(\cdot)$, and $\mathrm{ret}(E,q)$ exists for $E$ only. It therefore has no way to say what Engram, kNN-LM, PlugLM, ExplicitLM, MoE, MoBA and NSA have in common: capacity that grows by adding addressable slots rather than by growing a dense tensor. This matters most at ch29, whose whole argument is about where memory traffic lands — and sparse addressing is precisely a memory-device story the monograph currently cannot name.

UPDATE-RULE GRANULARITY (Table II). The monograph's (U-W) covers both a closed-form delta-rule state transition (no backward pass) and a gradient inner loop (a backward pass per chunk). Those differ by roughly a factor of three in FLOPs and they differ in whether an optimizer state must be held. The survey separates them ('state-transition updates' vs 'optimization-based writing') and attaches different risks to each. For a book whose thesis is cost accounting this is a distinction the monograph should have and does not. Same point for (U-E), which covers both 'an LLM re-reasons and rewrites a text block' and 'evict the stale entry'; the survey's row 4 separates them.

SIGNAL-GATED WRITING AS A NAMED CATEGORY. Table II row 3 (Titans, GDWM, AMOR, HAM) names write-admission control as a first-class mechanism family. The monograph's recurring complaint across ch14/ch15/ch27 is that nothing in the corpus verifies or gates its writes. The survey shows that the $W$-layer community has been building exactly those gates since 2026. ch27 and ch30 are weaker without this.

AN EXTERNAL POSITIONING TABLE. Table III (p.6) enumerates five prior memory taxonomies and their organizing lenses. ch01 and ch11 can use it to establish, from an outside source, that no existing taxonomy uses update timing relative to the query.
axis_contrast_with_book.verdict: [평가] The survey is a better map of the $W$ layer's 2026 frontier and of read-side addressing; the monograph is a better instrument for the question 'does spending compute before the query pay'. They are not competitors for the same question, and the honest statement in ch11 is that the survey's axes and the discriminant are ORTHOGONAL INSTRUMENTS with almost disjoint corpora — 3 shared papers out of 29 and 85 references. The one place where the monograph must concede ground is read-side structure, and the concession is owed at ch26 and ch29, not at ch11.

nested_learning_classification.question: ch18 判定: 'Nested Learning (2512.24695) | 모든 갱신이 (U-W). $\Theta$는 아무것도 안 움직이는 $f=0$ 끝점. 연속체는 표기의 다리이지 기제의 다리가 아니다' [PRE-RESEARCH §2.2]. Does this survey's classification of NL as a multi-timescale mechanism conflict with that verdict?
nested_learning_classification.verdict: NO CONFLICT. The survey classifies NL as multi-timescale, but every timescale it names lives among memory parameters / fast weights, and it puts the backbone OUTSIDE the hierarchy in its own words. ch18's verdict is corroborated, not threatened. There is a residual RHETORICAL friction over two unevidenced labels ('Explicit', 'Long-Term'), recorded below.

where_the_survey_places_NL.assignment: Update Dynamics = Online; Persistence = Long-Term; Main Paradigm = 'Multi-Timescale Updated Modules'; Year 2025
where_the_survey_places_NL.note: column alignment verified independently twice — see todo_verify T1

where_the_survey_places_NL.assignment: listed with TTT-E2E [9], Titans [8], In-Place TTT [48]. The row's mechanism definition is 'Memory parameters or FAST WEIGHTS are updated by minimizing an explicit objective, either during training or at inference time.' Risk column: 'Drift, instability, and objective mismatch'.
where_the_survey_places_NL.note: DECISIVE. The survey's own word for NL's substrate is 'memory parameters or fast weights' — the monograph's $W$ — and its three companions in that row are the three canonical fast-weight/TTT methods.

where_the_survey_places_NL.quote: 'Nested Learning [11] further extends this paradigm by introducing multi-frequency update schedules, where different parameter subsets evolve at distinct temporal scales. Across these methods, the defining feature remains consistent: memory is instantiated as one or a few parameterized modules whose updates are temporally and functionally separable from the static base model weights.'
where_the_survey_places_NL.note: 'separable from the STATIC base model weights' — the survey states that the base weights are static. That is $\Theta$ frozen, i.e. ch18's $f=0$ endpoint, in the survey's own prose.

where_the_survey_places_NL.quote: 'Nested Learning [11] generalizes this idea by introducing hierarchically organized update frequencies. Different parameter subsets operate under distinct learning rates and update schedules, creating a layered structure of fast-adapting and slow-adapting components. Rather than a binary distinction between backbone and memory, nested update mechanisms form a spectrum of temporal plasticity.'
where_the_survey_places_NL.note: This is the sentence that looks most like a challenge to ch18 — 'a spectrum of temporal plasticity', 'rather than a binary distinction between backbone and memory'. But read exactly: the spectrum is over PARAMETER SUBSETS with distinct learning rates and schedules. Nothing here says the backbone is one of those subsets. Under (U-W) this is $\{W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(m)}\}$ with distinct $\eta^{(j)}$ and distinct update periods — a frequency-indexed family of (U-W), which is exactly ch18's reading.

where_the_survey_places_NL.quote: 'For example, End-to-End Test-Time Training (TTT-E2E) [9] performs batch-style parameter updates during inference, whereas Nested Learning [11] decomposes learning into multiple nested optimization loops operating at distinct frequencies. When integrated into larger architectures, these mechanisms create memory hierarchies in which activation states evolve at token-level granularity, explicit memory modules update at interaction or batch level, and BACKBONE PARAMETERS REMAIN FROZEN OR ADAPT SLOWLY.'
where_the_survey_places_NL.note: THE CLOSING ARGUMENT. When the survey spells out what an NL-style hierarchy contains, it gives three tiers and assigns the backbone to 'frozen or adapt slowly' — with no mechanism, no citation, and no example for the 'adapt slowly' branch. That is ch18's $f=0$ endpoint, restated by an independent 2026 survey.

what_the_survey_never_says: It never claims Nested Learning updates the pretrained backbone. Not in Table I, not in Table II, not in §IV-A-b, not in §IV-D-b, not in §V-A-d.

It never gives NL an offline/sleep phase. NL is 'Online' in Table I, and the survey's 'online' means during inference. So under the survey's own axis NL updates DURING the request — which is condition (1) of the discriminant failing, stated by the survey.

It gives no evidence for either of the two labels the monograph would contest ('Explicit', 'Long-Term'). No persistence experiment, no cross-session claim, no capacity number, no citation to an NL result. The labels are asserted in a table cell.
the_residual_friction_recorded_honestly: The survey grants NL the label EXPLICIT MEMORY. In monograph terms NL's states are internal module parameters with no independent addressing interface at inference — the survey's own criterion for implicit. The criterion it actually applies is 'designed and operated as memory' (design intent), which NL satisfies by self-description. ch18 should note that the promotion is definitional, not mechanistic, and that the same criterion put Titans in explicit and Mamba in implicit despite (U-W) covering both.

The survey grants NL the label LONG-TERM. Under the survey's own definition ('extended effective horizon... rather than storage size alone', §II-C-b, p.5) this claims only an unbounded receptive field, not cross-session survival — and 37 of 47 systems carry it. But the survey's §III-D-c states the opposite about a sibling mechanism: cached recurrent snapshots 'primarily improve retention within an extended sequence rather than introducing fully persistent memory across sessions [27], [37]' [p.9]. If that reasoning applies to Memory Caching it applies to NL, and the Long-Term label is inconsistent with it.

The survey does NOT reproduce NL's own continuum claim (that optimizers, attention and architectures are all the same object at different update frequencies). It takes the weaker part — different subsets, different frequencies — and drops the identification. ch18's finding that 'the continuum is a bridge of notation, not of mechanism' is therefore neither confirmed nor contradicted by the survey; the survey simply declines to carry the strong claim forward. That declining is itself mild evidence for ch18.
nested_learning_classification.net_effect_on_ch18: CONFIRMS. ch18 gains an external, independent, non-adversarial classification that (i) files NL alongside TTT-E2E / Titans / In-Place TTT, (ii) calls its substrate 'memory parameters or fast weights', and (iii) explicitly leaves the backbone frozen. ch18 should quote §V-A-d p.15 and §IV-A-b p.10. It should also record the two unevidenced labels as an instance of how easily a frequency hierarchy over $W$ is written up as a two-layer memory system — which is precisely the reading error ch18 exists to prevent.

cost_reporting_treatment.question: X3 established that of the monograph's 29 corpus papers exactly one reports $B_s$ in absolute units, and PRE-RESEARCH §4 records 'corpus 전체에서 상태 용량을 바이트로 보고한 논문이 0편이다'. Does this survey register that vacuum, or pass over it?
cost_reporting_treatment.verdict: PARTIAL — it names the desideratum three times and never instantiates it once, and it diagnoses the wrong disease. The survey's complaint is that current evaluation CONFLATES memory with reasoning and scale; it never observes that the papers it reviews do not report cost at all. It proposes four evaluation axes and gives no unit for any of them. And because its update axis has no pre-query cell, the specific quantity X3 is about ($B_s$) is not merely unreported but unaskable in its frame.

what_it_does_say.quote: 'Memory evaluation must also account for computational and storage cost. Extended context performance can be artificially inflated by increasing window size, yet such gains may be impractical under real-world memory constraints. Recent benchmarks therefore report performance as a function of context length and memory footprint, emphasizing scaling curves rather than single-point metrics.'
what_it_does_say.reading: asserts that benchmarks DO report memory footprint. No benchmark is named for this and no such curve is reproduced.

Future work may benefit from decomposing memory performance into orthogonal axes—capacity, fidelity, persistence, and efficiency—allowing systematic comparison across implicit, explicit, and hybrid architectures.'

P1_fills_a_named_hole.survey_claim: 'introduce periodic processing of cached representations, using an auxiliary bottleneck module to consolidate or rewrite parts of the working memory at structured generation boundaries' [§V-B-c, p.15]
P1_fills_a_named_hole.why_it_matters: The closest thing in the survey to a CONSOLIDATION operator over the wake-time state. It is mid-query, so it fails condition (1) — but it is the mechanism a $W$-path sleep phase would need, and ch17/ch18 currently have no comparison point for it.

P1_fills_a_named_hole.survey_claim: 'a fixed-size latent memory pool embedded across Transformer layers and refreshed through forward-only self-updates when new knowledge is read. Unlike gradient-based test-time adaptation, such updates directly rewrite dedicated memory tokens while keeping the backbone unchanged' [§IV-A-b, p.10]
P1_fills_a_named_hole.why_it_matters: A FIXED-SIZE self-updating store with a forward-only write — structurally between $W$ and $E$, and it predates the whole corpus (2024). If its write is genuinely knowledge-triggered rather than per-token it may be a discriminant boundary case.

P1_fills_a_named_hole.paper: ExplicitLM — decoupling knowledge from parameters via explicit memory banks
P1_fills_a_named_hole.survey_claim: 'layer-wise explicit memory banks whose entries are human-readable token sequences and are accessed through a two-stage differentiable retrieval mechanism' [§IV-B-d, p.12]
P1_fills_a_named_hole.why_it_matters: An $E$-shaped store (human-readable text) placed INSIDE the architecture. The monograph's three layers assume text stores are outside the model; this is a counterexample the frame has to absorb or explicitly exclude.

P1_fills_a_named_hole.survey_claim: 'reinterpreting feed-forward networks as context-free token-wise retrieval modules... enabling their outputs to be precomputed as token-level lookups' [§IV-B-e, p.12]
P1_fills_a_named_hole.why_it_matters: PRECOMPUTATION as an architecture. Under the discriminant it fails the same way Memory Layers fails (a one-time build artefact, not a per-deployment write), which is a useful confirmation that the discriminant is stable — and it is a 2026 capacity-supply source for ch09.

P2_context_and_falsification.paper: Muon-OGD (spectral orthogonal gradient projection for LLM continual learning)
P2_context_and_falsification.why_it_matters: A 2026 continual-learning optimizer aimed at interference under repeated parameter updates — i.e. a candidate mitigation for the $\rho$ that ch22's falsification axis is built on. The survey's own framing: 'as more architectures introduce writable parameter subsets, the geometry of the update rule may become as important as the storage form itself for preventing drift' [§IV-E-f, p.13].

P2_context_and_falsification.paper: Orthogonal low-rank adaptation in Lie groups for continual learning of LLMs
P2_context_and_falsification.why_it_matters: same axis as above; also a LoRA-family result that ch19 does not have

P2_context_and_falsification.why_it_matters: 'Complementary memory systems' is CLS vocabulary and Gershman is a computational cognitive scientist — this may be the rare architecture paper that carries the CLS argument rather than borrowing the word. open_questions.question: Is there a unifying formal theory of memory in LLMs?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Current memory mechanisms are often categorized operationally—attention, recurrence, retrieval, parametric—without a unifying formal theoretical abstraction. However, these mechanisms can be interpreted within a broader state-transition perspective, where memory differs primarily in persistence, accessibility, update dynamics, and representational compression.'
open_questions.bridge_out: the survey's own abstract claims to 'formalize the granular mechanisms'; §VI-A says the formalization does not exist. See unfavorable_facts F2.

open_questions.question: How can lifelong parametric memory avoid forgetting and instability?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Gradient-based test-time updates, nested parameter hierarchies, and modular memory blocks blur the distinction between pretraining and inference. However, these mechanisms also reintroduce classical challenges of continual learning, including forgetting and instability under distribution shift... Achieving scalable lifelong memory without full retraining remains one of the central open problems in large-scale model design.'
open_questions.bridge_out: this is the monograph's $\rho$ and its ch22 falsification axis, named from the $W$-layer side

open_questions.question: Can update rules be made diagnosable and reversible?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Admission, eviction, and consolidation rules face a related irreversibility problem: once a token or memory entry is dropped, compressed, or overwritten, later retrieval may be impossible. A key future direction is therefore to develop update rules that are not only efficient, but also diagnosable, reversible when necessary, and robust under long-horizon distribution shifts.'
open_questions.bridge_out: independent external naming of the flaw ch14 identifies in Letta's destructive $\mathrm{wr}$

open_questions.question: Who allocates traffic across coexisting memory pathways?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Most existing models rely on static compositions, where memory pathways are fixed at design time. This rigidity limits the ability to adapt memory usage to task structure or contextual demands. A promising direction lies in adaptive memory orchestration. Learned controllers may dynamically allocate tokens across memory subsystems...'
open_questions.bridge_out: structurally the same missing controller Letta STC names in its own §7 ('optimally allocating inference compute between sleep-time and test-time'), reached from the architecture side instead of the serving side. Two paths independently arrive at 'nobody has written the allocator'.

open_questions.question: What does hardware-algorithm co-design for memory look like?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'As context windows extend to hundreds of thousands or millions of tokens, memory bandwidth and storage hierarchies increasingly dominate system performance. Architectural innovation can no longer be decoupled from hardware constraints. Future models may integrate hierarchical memory designs aligned with GPU and accelerator memory tiers, enabling multi-level caching and selective recomputation. In-memory attention computation and hardware-aware sparsity patterns suggest that memory operations themselves may become primary computational primitives.'
open_questions.bridge_out: the closest external statement to the monograph's memory-device thesis — and entirely unevidenced. See systems_implications.

open_questions.question: How should memory be measured?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'evaluation of memory systems remains fragmented and not targeted. Most current protocols measure performance under extended context lengths, yet this conflates memory capacity with reasoning ability and other scaling effects. A more principled evaluation paradigm would decompose memory performance into orthogonal dimensions, including storage capacity, retrieval fidelity, temporal persistence, robustness to interference, and computational efficiency.'
open_questions.bridge_out: supports the PREMISE of ch25/ch26 and supplies no unit. See cost_reporting_treatment.

open_questions.question: Where exactly is the boundary between explicit fast-weight memory and implicit sequence dynamics?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'the boundary between explicit fast-weight memory and implicit sequence dynamics should be drawn carefully. Recent analysis of TTT with key–value binding argues that a broad class of such inner-loop updates can be reformulated as learned linear attention [72].'
open_questions.bridge_out: the survey states, as an open problem, that its own primary axis is not well-defined at the point where the monograph's $W$ layer lives. Highest-value pointer in the paper.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The survey's PRIMARY axis rests on design intent, and the survey concedes in its own text that the criterion breaks under a reduction result.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: explicit memory is distinguished 'not [by] their parametric form, but the fact that they are designed and operated as memory' [§II-A-b, p.2]; then 'Recent analysis of TTT with key–value binding argues that a broad class of such inner-loop updates can be reformulated as learned linear attention [72]. This does not invalidate the memory interpretation of TTT-style modules, but it suggests that only variants with a clearly designated, autonomously updated storage substrate should be treated as explicit memory in the main taxonomy.' [§IV-A-c, p.11]
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the retreat position — 'clearly designated... storage substrate' — is packaging, not mechanism. Titans and Mamba end up on opposite sides of the top-level axis while instantiating the same update equation.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The abstract claims a formalization that §VI-A says does not exist.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: Abstract: 'We further formalize the granular mechanisms dictating memory writing, routing, state transitions, and consolidation.' §VI-A: 'Current memory mechanisms are often categorized operationally—attention, recurrence, retrieval, parametric—without a unifying formal theoretical abstraction.' The 'formalization' delivered is Table II's five prose descriptions. The paper contains exactly one numbered equation, Eq. (1), and it is MoE gating — a read, not a write.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: a paper whose contribution is a frame states in its own conclusions section that the frame has not been formalized

unfavorable_facts.fact: The claimed orthogonality of the three axes is falsified by the survey's own Table I.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'These three axes are largely orthogonal.' [§II-C-c, p.5]
unfavorable_facts.numbers: Of 47 rows: implicit systems are 29/30 = 96.7% Online; explicit systems are 10/17 = 58.8% Offline. Explicit systems are 17/17 = 100% Long-Term — there is not one Explicit/Short-Term entry. Three of the eight cells are empty (explicit-offline-short, explicit-online-short, implicit-offline-short). Persistence takes one value in 37 of 47 rows.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: representation predicts update dynamics almost deterministically in one direction and predicts persistence deterministically; an axis carrying one value 79% of the time discriminates little. Recomputed directly from the vendored table columns.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table I is single-label by admission, in a paper whose conclusion is that hybrids are the dominant trend.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: Table I caption: 'Note that all models are represented by their primary mechanism of memory, and some models may simultaneously encompass multiple features within the same axis.' §VII: 'modern LLM design is rapidly shifting toward hybrid architectures that adaptively orchestrate these complementary substrates.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the classification instrument is declared inadequate for exactly the class the paper says is winning. Jamba, Samba, Hydra, HAM, AMOR and Kimi Linear each get one cell.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Internal contradiction on persistence. §III-D-c denies cross-session persistence to the very systems Table I labels Long-Term.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Even mechanisms that enlarge effective recurrent capacity, such as cached state snapshots or mixtures of recurrent states, primarily improve retention within an extended sequence rather than introducing fully persistent memory across sessions [27], [37].' [§III-D-c, p.9]. Reference [37] is Memory Caching and [27] is MoM — both are labelled 'Long-Term' in Table I.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: if the reasoning holds for Memory Caching it holds for every fixed-size recurrent state in the table, and for Nested Learning. The Long-Term label is not doing the work its name implies.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Zero negative results about any cited system. No ablation reversal, no failed replication, no instance of a baseline beating a method, no limitation attributed to a named paper.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: every system is described in its own vocabulary and by its own claims. The only criticism in the paper is generic and lives in the 'Main Risks' column of Table II, where it is attached to a mechanism family rather than to any measurement or any paper. For the monograph this bounds how much the survey can be used: it is a coverage source, never an evaluative one.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper asserts a field-level trend with no evidence of any kind.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'memory is transitioning into a primary, explicit architectural design dimension rather than remaining a mere byproduct of scaling' [§I, p.1]; 'modern LLM design is rapidly shifting toward hybrid architectures' [§VII, p.18]
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: no adoption count, no deployment survey, no citation trend, no publication-volume argument is offered for 'transitioning' or 'rapidly'. The only quantitative substrate available is Table I, and Table I's own composition (30 implicit vs 17 explicit; 10 of 17 explicit rows are offline lookup/MoE) does not obviously support it.

unfavorable_facts.fact: It claims 'Recent benchmarks therefore report performance as a function of context length and memory footprint' and names no such benchmark.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the five benchmarks it does name — RULER [59], LongBench [83], ∞Bench [60], L-Eval [84], SCROLLS [85] — are accuracy benchmarks; none reports memory footprint. This is the one place where the survey makes a checkable empirical claim about the literature, and it supplies no instance.

unfavorable_facts.fact: It splits a single research programme across three sections and two top-level categories without noticing.
unfavorable_facts.detail: Titans [8], Nested Learning [11] and Memory Caching [37] share a first author (A. Behrouz) and largely the same coauthor set (Razaviyayn, Zhong, Mirrokni). The survey places Titans in §IV-A (explicit), Nested Learning in §IV-A + §IV-D (explicit), and Memory Caching in §III (implicit) + §V-B (efficiency), and never remarks on the shared lineage.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the paper's stated purpose is to 'reveal common structures underlying seemingly diverse methods' [§II, p.2]; missing a same-lab, same-year continuation is a miss on its own terms — and it is the same pair the monograph's ch18 treats as one chapter.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Two distinct papers named MemoryLLM appear in Table I, disambiguated only by capitalisation.
unfavorable_facts.detail: 'MEMORYLLM [44]' (Wang et al. 2024, 2402.04624, online latent memory pool) and 'MemoryLLM (FFN) [50]' (Jaiswal et al. 2026, 2602.00398, offline feed-forward lookup) — opposite update-dynamics labels, adjacent rows in the same table.
unfavorable_facts.mitigating: the prose DOES disambiguate them explicitly: 'This work is conceptually different from online self-updatable MEMORYLLM [44]' [§IV-B-e, p.12]. Credit where due; the table is the fragile part.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table III characterises five prior surveys entirely by their own self-descriptions, with no assessment of any of them.
unfavorable_facts.detail: The claim 'complementing rather than superseding system- and cognition-centered accounts' [§II-D, p.6] is asserted; no method is shown to be better placed by these axes than by a predecessor's.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the positioning table is the paper's argument for its own necessity, and it is argued by scope statement rather than by a worked case

unfavorable_facts.fact: The title and abstract are broader than the scope, and the scope restrictions arrive only inside §II and §IV.
unfavorable_facts.detail: Title: 'Memory for Large Language Models'. Abstract: 'a systematic, architecture-centric taxonomy of memory in LLMs'. The exclusions of agent/prompt memory (§II preamble, p.2) and pretrained parameters (§II-A-c, p.2) are not signalled in the title or abstract, and they remove the entire retrieval-agent literature and the entire weight-editing literature.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: a reader who stops at the abstract will believe RAG, agent memory, and model editing were surveyed and found unimportant; they were excluded by definition

unfavorable_facts.fact: It uses the biological word 'consolidation' eleven times with zero biological content and zero neuroscience citations.

cross_path_citations.verdict: Total silence toward the $E$-path and the $\Theta$-path, both by declared exclusion; deep and current coverage of the $W$-path, which is its home; and total silence toward biology, in a survey whose subject is memory and whose update-rule vocabulary is borrowed from the consolidation literature.

RAG is named only to be excluded: §IV-B-f 'Distinguishing Model-Level Retrieval from RAG' — 'RAG systems typically rely on external document corpora, vector databases, and orchestration pipelines that exist outside the model architecture. In contrast, the mechanisms discussed here embed persistent storage directly into the model's structural design.' [p.12]

This survey is external confirmation that the 2026 memory-architecture community does not make that reconstruction.

Combined with the E-path finding from ch14 (Letta STC's 22 references contain no biology either), this gives ch23 two independent, opposite-corner data points: the E-path borrowed the word 'sleep' without the biology, and the architecture community borrowed the word 'consolidation' without the biology.

items.grounding: [PAPER] §V-A-d, p.15: 'these mechanisms create memory hierarchies in which activation states evolve at token-level granularity, explicit memory modules update at interaction or batch level, and backbone parameters remain frozen or adapt slowly.' Three update rates — token, interaction/batch, never — with the storage class named at each. That is the shape ch29 argues for, written by an architecture-side author.

items.claim: The one cost distinction the survey draws that the monograph's cost vector cannot: a gradient write costs a backward pass, a state-transition write does not.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table II rows 1-2, p.5 (optimization-based writing vs state-transition updates). [INFERENCE] For a serving fleet these differ by roughly the usual forward:backward ratio and, more importantly, by whether optimizer state must be resident. The monograph's $B_s$ is a scalar in FLOPs-or-tokens and hides both. ch25 should either split $B_s$ by write kind or state explicitly that it does not.

items.claim: Sparse addressing is a memory-device story the monograph's frame currently cannot name.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §IV-B-c, p.12: Engram provides 'a scalable addressing substrate whose capacity can grow independently from dense computation, subject to the accuracy and collision behavior of the indexing scheme'; §IV-B-g, p.12: 'storage capacity scales with the number of slots or datastore size, rather than being bounded by fixed hidden dimensions.' [INFERENCE] A large, sparsely-read, collision-managed table addressed per token is a capacity-over-bandwidth device profile — different from both the E-path (text into a database) and the Theta-path (weight delta into device memory) that ch29 currently contrasts. The monograph's read equation (R) hides this inside $f(\cdot)$.

items.claim: The survey's own systems section is thin and adds no numbers the monograph does not already have.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §V-B, pp.15-16 covers KV compression (CommVQ [81]), PagedAttention [82], Bottlenecked Transformers [51], sliding window vs sparse global. All qualitative — no compression ratio, no memory saving, no throughput figure. ch29 gains vocabulary, not evidence.

items.claim: For the monograph reader's standing question — 'so what changes at decode?' — this paper's answer is: nothing, because it describes no deployment. What it does supply is a map of where OTHER people's state lives at decode.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE], grounded in outer_vs_inner. the_reverse_application_which_is_the_use.question: Apply the monograph's discriminant to the survey's 47 tabulated systems. How many pass?
the_reverse_application_which_is_the_use.answer: ZERO, judged from the survey's own descriptions.
reasoning: The 36 'Online' entries fail condition (1). The survey's own definition of online is 'updates during inference... per token, per segment, or per batch' [§II-B-b, p.4] — every one of those is during a request, not before it.

The 11 'Offline' entries fail condition (1) in the other direction: they are 'updated only during a distinct model training phase' [§II-B-a, pp.3-4], i.e. before deployment rather than between requests, and they are not re-run per context.

The two entries that need explicit handling are Engram [10] and MemoryLLM (FFN) [50], whose stores are built before any query. Both fail on the same ground the monograph already used twice: on RAG in ch10 ('$S(c;B_s)$가 추론을 하지 않음' — the offline procedure performs no inference over the context) and on Memory Layers in ch11/ch09 ('배포 후 어떤 층도 안 바뀜. pre-training 1회'). They are one-time build artefacts, not per-deployment writes. Flagged in todo_verify T6 because this rests on the survey's description, not on the papers.
Bottlenecked Transformers [51] performs consolidation 'at structured generation boundaries' [§V-B-c, p.15] — mid-query, so condition (1) fails.
the_reverse_application_which_is_the_use.what_it_establishes: The monograph's discriminant, applied to a 47-system 2026 census of LLM memory assembled by people with no interest in the sleep-time question, returns zero. That is a strong, checkable statement of how narrow the category actually is, and it belongs in ch24. It also tightens ch11: the discriminant does not merely thin a corpus that was assembled around the word 'sleep' — it also excludes essentially the whole architecture-side memory literature, and for a single reason (condition (1)) rather than for scattered ones.
the_reverse_application_which_is_the_use.one_place_the_discriminant_shows_a_seam: Condition (2) as written ('a budget $B_s>0$ is spent') is satisfied by any precomputation, including building a kNN datastore or precomputing FFN lookups. What actually does the excluding is that $S(\cdot;B_s)$ must perform INFERENCE over the context — stated in ch10's treatment of RAG but not in the discriminant text itself. ch11 should make that explicit rather than leave it to be inferred, because this survey supplies four new systems that probe exactly that seam (kNN-LM, Engram, ExplicitLM, MemoryLLM-FFN).

More broadly, the monograph's read equation (R) hides all addressing inside $f(\cdot)$ and gives $\mathrm{ret}(\cdot,q)$ to $E$ alone, so the entire sparse-addressing design space is invisible in the monograph's frame — and sparse addressing is precisely the memory-device story ch29 is trying to tell.
